title: Projective envelope of a finite affine-space model
statement: Let $B$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme; def-weil-affine-spectrum] and let $d\ge0$. If $T\to\mathbf A^d_B$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] is a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], then there exist a scheme $P$ [def-pc-scheme], an open immersion $j:T\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a projective and proper morphism $p:P\to B$ [def-pc-projective-morphism; def-weil-proper-morphism] such that $p\circ j$ is the given structural morphism. Moreover every scheme-theoretic fibre of $p$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version: Zariski-main finite factorization followed by projective compactification; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose an affine presentation $B=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and put $Q=\mathbf P^d_B$, with structure map $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], its standard opens $Q_i=D_+(X_i)$, $0\le i\le d$, cover $Q$ and are affine spaces of dimension $d$ over $B$. The polynomial coordinates identify $Q_0$ with $\mathbf A^d_B$ of [def-nagata-relative-affine-space]. Write $u:\mathbf A^d_B\hookrightarrow Q$ for this open chart. The projection $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. In particular it is quasi-compact and separated, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] shows that $Q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The source $\mathbf A^d_B=\operatorname{Spec}A[z_1,\ldots,z_d]$ of $u$ is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; since its target $Q$ is quasi-separated, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] shows that $u$ is quasi-compact. (Concretely, $u^{-1}(Q_i)$ is the principal open of $Q_0$ where $X_i/X_0$ is invertible.)

source.place: Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space); affine chart calculation; properness Tag 01WC

proof.text: Let $h:T\to\mathbf A^d_B$ be the given finite morphism and set $f=u\circ h:T\to Q$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $h$ is affine; since $\mathbf A^d_B$ is affine, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $T$ affine. Hence $f$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. By [pqf-lem-finite-qf], $h$ is quasi-finite, in particular of finite type. The quasi-compact open immersion $u$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], so [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] makes $f$ of finite type. Over a point of $Q_0$ the fibre of $f$ is the corresponding fibre of $h$, while over a point outside $Q_0$ it is empty: this follows by pulling back the open-subscheme identification in [def-weil-open-immersion]. Every point of each fibre is therefore isolated by the quasi-finiteness of $h$. This is exactly quasi-finiteness of $f$ by clause (3) of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Moreover $f$ is quasi-finite at every point in the sense of clause (1): write $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$; then $U=T$ and the affine open $V=Q_0=\operatorname{Spec}A[z_1,\ldots,z_d]$ of $Q$ satisfy $f(U)\subset V$, the ring map $A[z_1,\ldots,z_d]\to C$ is module-finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] (as $h^{-1}(\mathbf A^d_B)=T$), and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite] makes it of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $C$. So $f$ is everywhere quasi-finite in either reading of the hypothesis of [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization].

source.place: Tag 05K0 (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite), checking its hypotheses for the standard affine chart

proof.text: Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to $f:T\to Q$. Step 1 supplies the required quasi-compact and quasi-separated target, and Step 2 supplies separatedness, finite type and quasi-finiteness. We obtain a scheme $P$, a quasi-compact open immersion $j:T\hookrightarrow P$, and a finite morphism $r:P\to Q$ with $r\circ j=f$. Define $p=q\circ r$. Finiteness makes $r$ proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]; properness of $q$ from [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] make $p$ proper. The factorization equation gives $p\circ j=q\circ u\circ h$, which is the given structural morphism of $T$ over $B$.

source.place: Tag 05K0 (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite); properness of finite maps and composition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] with $X=Q$ and the identity closed immersion into $\mathbf P^d_A$. It gives an ample invertible sheaf on $Q$, without any Noetherian hypothesis on $A$. By [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle], the finite map $r$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense. Since its target $Q$ admits that ample sheaf, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] makes $r$ H-projective. The projection $q$ is H-projective by [def-kun-projective], using the identity embedding of $Q$ into $\mathbf P^d_B$. Therefore [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] makes $p=q\circ r$ H-projective. Step 3 already proves $p$ proper, hence quasi-compact; together with H-projectivity this is projectivity in exactly the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism].

Fix $b\in B$ and put $k=\kappa(b)$. The fibre $P_b$ is $P\times_Q Q_b$, where $Q_b=\mathbf P^d_k$, by the fibre-product universal property and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. Thus $r_b:P_b\to Q_b$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. The standard charts $V_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}k[z_1,\ldots,z_d]$ cover $Q_b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Their inverse images $W_i=r_b^{-1}(V_i)$ cover $P_b$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], each $W_i$ is affine, say $\operatorname{Spec}C_i$, and $k[z_1,\ldots,z_d]\to C_i$ is module-finite. The same module generators, together with the images of the $d$ polynomial variables, generate $C_i$ as a $k$-algebra: any element is a polynomial-coefficient linear combination of the module generators. In particular $C_i$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra.

source.place: Finite base change, Tag 01WK (lemma-base-change-finite); standard projective charts Tag 01NG

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-map-quasi-finite], each module-finite map $k[z_1,\ldots,z_d]\to C_i$ from Step 5 is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime. All hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra] therefore hold with $n=d$, and it gives $\dim W_i\le d$. This allows noninjective coefficient maps and zero algebras; no surjectivity of $r_b$ is needed. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], the underlying space of the scheme $P_b$ is sober, hence quasi-sober and $T_0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-bound-open-cover] to the open cover $(W_i)_{0\le i\le d}$ to obtain $\dim P_b\le d$. Since $b$ was arbitrary, every scheme-theoretic fibre has the asserted bound. Empty fibres have dimension $-\infty$ and cause no exception.
